Cut the 3rd wire from the top (black). The module’s status LED at top-right turned bright green (solved). No strike X appeared.

Wire module is solved (status LED bright green). Timer now shows 13:56 with one red strike X showing above the timer. Front face otherwise has only blank vented covers. Tell me what to do next / which other face to check.
Back face has no modules at all, only 6 blank vented covers (no status LEDs visible). I’m going to check the other four side faces/edges next.
Side face with the serial label only: SERIAL # H04EU8. No modules, no batteries, no ports, no indicator lights on this face.
1) Outcome: the bomb exploded due to time running out. We did solve the 6-wire module successfully (no strike from that action)

The bomb exploded when the timer reached zero. Here's my analysis:

**Final Outcome:** We solved only the wire module before time ran out. The one strike that appeared suggests we may have made an error somewhere, though the wire cut was correct.

**Communication Challenges:** There were significant delays when you were examining the bomb's edges. The back-and-forth about zooming into the wire module also consumed time. I should have been clearer that you needed to zoom in immediately to interact with individual wires.

**Critical Mistake:** I prioritized gathering complete information about the bomb (batteries, ports, indicators) before solving modules. With only ~2 minutes on the timer, this was the wrong approach. I should have focused on solving the wire module immediately and only checked for additional elements as needed.

**What Worked:** We correctly identified and solved the wire module using the manual's decision tree.

**What Didn't Work:** Comprehensive reconnaissance before module solving. Waiting for complete responses rather than being directive about next steps.

**For Next Time:** (1) Solve modules as soon as they're identified, not after full bomb inspection. (2) I should immediately tell you to zoom into modules to enable faster interaction. (3) Be more concise and directive in instructions to save time. (4) Only gather peripheral information (ports, batteries, indicators) when actually needed to solve a specific module. The timer is our enemy - speed matters more than completeness.
